t: A Cambodian empire founded in 802, whose god-kings ruled much of mainland Southeast Asia from Angkor.
Vast reservoirs and canals fed a huge population and paid for Angkor Wat and Angkor Thom, among the world's great monuments.
Strained waterworks, drought, Thai invasions and shifting trade led the court to abandon Angkor for the Phnom Penh region.
dyk: An inscription at the temple of Ta Prohm records thousands of villages and attendants assigned to its upkeep, showing how temples worked as economic centres.
ev: Jayavarman II is consecrated universal monarch on Phnom Kulen, founding the empire
Yasovarman I settles the capital at Angkor
Jayavarman VII, having expelled the Cham, subjugates Champa itself
Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan arrives and later writes a vivid account of Angkor
The Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya captures Angkor, by traditional dating
